svg.title: OpenGrid dispatch stack and 2-second real-time cycle
svg.text: OpenGrid Orchestrator — Dispatch Stack and the 2-Second Real-Time Cycle
Selector (MILP/LP) → real-time allocator → ledger → guardian sign → MQTT → hub → ack/telemetry → settle, as implemented on main @ f3b3365
implemented stage
guardian check
ledger / Postgres write
MQTT
planned / not driven by any caller
1. Selector — day-ahead / intraday planning gate
opengrid.selector — gate.py, model.py, solve.py, rule_fallback.py
Trigger (opengrid.engine.GateScheduler, run every og-engine tick):
• SCHEDULED_15MIN — wall-clock 15-min tick (once/day at 00:05, plan_mode=L-DA; else L-ID)
• ADMISSION — a new opportunity whose contract can't wait for the next 15-min tick
• RENOMINATION — a contract's due renomination_point (that obligation only, K13)
engine.gates.run_due_gates() catches each trigger's own exception — traced +
ALR-SELECTOR-GATE-FAILED, tick continues for every other trigger (K7). start_gates_in_
background() (NEW, f3b3365) now runs the whole gate batch as ONE background task, never
awaited by the 2 s tick — a 24 h gate (capability load, intake, LP) took 10-20 s and held
dispatch for committed obligations that long (A11 p99, live 2026-09-26); triggers arriving
mid-run wait in a de-duplicated backlog. og-engine's own cycle latency (p50/p99/max over a
150-tick/~5min window) is traced as CYCLE_LATENCY — target A11 “p99 < 500ms at 2k hubs”,
metric exists, target not yet proven met at that scale (still open).
build_mode_o_model (HiGHS, “Mode O”): BINARY / CONTINUOUS / SEMI_CONTINUOUS vars per
candidate; C1 energy balance + C2 SoC bounds (banks carrying an energy envelope); C6/C13
one shared bank/interval capacity row (K2 one-buyer); C12 firm delivery + eligible-bank
locality; C15 terminal-energy floor; C16 non-anticipativity; C24 commitment-lock equality
on each COMMITTED/DELIVERING obligation's total (never re-decided — diagram 03)
highs_solve → extract_plan → validate_plan. On INFEASIBLE_F1 / TIME_LIMIT_GAP / an
invalid solution → rule_fallback_f2 (greedy, no solver: committed first, then candidates
FIRM > AS > MARKET by richest $/MWh — also the KPI-22 baseline the LP is measured against).
LP plans are LIVE again (FIXED, 927cc77): the bank charge envelope is now passed to the model
(previously omitted, so it could never recharge — every plan fell back to F2, live 2026-09-26)
and fleet.capability() is read ONCE per bank, not once per bank/interval (was ~96x redundant
reads/gate). Soft C15 (penalized terminal-energy target, not a hard floor) avoids the
infeasibility a hard floor caused. Applies to both L-DA and L-ID plan modes.
persist_plan → og.plan → per selected candidate: selector.commit.commit_candidate()
drives OFFERED→SELECTED→COMMITTED (or →REJECTED) around ledger.reserve(); every UNselected
candidate above fleet capacity → reject_structurally_infeasible() (NEW, 289d68f), R-ADMIT-
REJECT, traced — both record an opportunity decision (SELECTED/REJECTED) too (diagram 03)
SCED-interval LP (5-min re-pricing)
02a §3.1 (spec) explicitly folds this into
the real-time allocator's per-cycle price
response, stage 2 ▸S6 below — there is no
separate 5-min solve in the code.
every 2 s (allocator.cycle_interval_s)
2. Real-time allocator — 2 s cycle
opengrid.allocator.cycle.cycle() — pure function, run per bank
S1 ·K5 _apply_instructions: an active L2 utility/ISO instruction (LIMIT/BLOCK/ESTOP)
caps the bank's capability first — hard, never traded for commercial value
S2 ·K1 _cap_sustainable_discharge: each hub's free_discharge_kw is capped by the ENERGY
sustainable over the command's LEASE TTL, not just this tick; missing/stale SoC
→ 0 kW (never trusted at face value)
S3 allocate_tiers: T1 → T2 → T3 → T4, greedy in strict order (the lexicographic
optimum for one scalar resource); a tier that can't get its committed_kw is
reported as a shortfall on that SAME obligation (R-COMMIT-LOCK-INFEASIBLE or,
under an active L2 instruction, R-COMMIT-LOCK-OVERRIDE-L2) — never reassigned
S4 ·K9 DistDeferralPI: exactly ONE integrator per bank, stepped once per cycle; its
relief kW tops up that bank's first DIST_DEFERRAL call (R-GRANT-DIST-DEFERRAL-PI)
S5 realize_obligation: water_fill (weighted by free_discharge_kw × tau, 20% stickiness
bonus for hubs served last cycle) across an obligation's ELIGIBLE hubs, excluding
unhealthy ones → SubstitutionEvent (R-SUBSTITUTION), now traced (ledger.record_
substitution_events, NEW) when a healthy hub took over
S6 leftover bank headroom → price_responsive_schedule: 5-min dwell + $5/MWh hysteresis
→ R-GRANT-HEADROOM (uncommitted, priced to ERCOT_ENERGY only above threshold)
S7 persist_grants → og.grant (insert-only; one fresh row set every cycle)
In parallel, every cycle (K1)
EnergySufficiencyGateway.run() (engine/
gateways.py): every COMMITTED/DELIVERING
obligation's remaining energy vs. reserve
on its hubs, net of other obligations'
claims on the same bank.
AT_RISK → og.obligation_energy_status +
og.obligation.at_risk (NEW, 01fbd38: set
True on entry, False on recovery, via
contracts.set_obligation_at_risk()) + trace
+ ALR-ENERGY-SHORTFALL-RISK on entry only.
Sustained (60s) infeasibility after substi-
tution also escalates DELIVERING→SHORTFALL
(engine.escalation, NEW — diagram 03).
Never reallocates capacity itself (K13).
3. Ledger — reservations
opengrid.ledger.ReservationLedger — single writer per og-engine process
K2 one-buyer (reserve, at selection time): per bank/interval, sum(active reservations) +
the new amount must not exceed fleet.capability() — else ReservationError(
"R-COMMIT-LOCK-INFEASIBLE") with no partial writes across the obligation's intervals
K13 commitment lock (release / reduce / substitute): a committed reservation may only be
reduced with an allowed reason — R-COMMIT-LOCK-OVERRIDE-L0/L1/L2, R-COMMIT-LOCK-INFEASIBLE,
R-FULFILLED, R-SETTLED, R-SUBSTITUTION, or the disabled-by-default R-AS-RELEASE. substitute()
moves a reservation to a different bank for the SAME obligation, total preserved.
Commitment path (FIXED, 9e1859f+289d68f)
selector.commit.commit_candidate() drives
OFFERED → SELECTED → COMMITTED (or →
REJECTED) through contracts.transition_
obligation; ledger.reserve() writes
og.commitment atomically with og.
reservation (build_commitments()).
NEW this round: settle.close_settled_
obligations() now drives FULFILLED/
SHORTFALL → SETTLED (R-SETTLED) — the
prior residual gap is closed. Only
R-COMMIT-LOCK-OVERRIDE-L0/-L1 (mid-window
device/homeowner overrides) still have 0
callers; the L2/INFEASIBLE mid-window path
is coded + wired but not yet observed
firing live (diagram 03).
engine → guardian (Postgres-mediated, K10)
4. Engine → Guardian handoff
opengrid.engine.propose_batch_to_guardian() — Postgres as the queue
build_command_batch_row: merkle_root = SHA-256 over the JCS-canonical grant list for this
bank/cycle; trace_pre_image_id is REQUIRED (K10: no command is signed unless its decision
pre-image is already durably traced)
ORDER matters: trace.append("RT_ALLOCATION") commits FIRST → then INSERT og.command_batch
(carrying that same trace_id) → then NOTIFY og_command_batch. og-guardian is woken only
after its pre-image already exists.
_distribute_hub_items (engine/__init__.py) applies RAMP_SAFETY_FACTOR=0.9 via apply_ramp_
limit (core.physics.hub_ramp_kw_per_s, NEW — the SAME bound guardian's G-04 checks) before
building each hub's setpoint, so the engine never proposes a step guardian would veto
5. Guardian verdict + Ed25519 signing (sole signer, K3)
opengrid.guardian.service.GuardianService — guardian/checks.py
GuardianService.evaluate_and_sign (guardian/service.py): G-20 runs FIRST and ALONE (every
other freshness/lease check depends on the guardian's own clock); every other check then
accumulates independently — one veto never hides another. G-14 short-circuits the rest if
the trace pre-image is missing (nothing downstream is trustworthy without it).
Outcome: PASS (signs) · PARTLY_VETOED (only item-level rules, a strict hub subset) ·
VETOED (a batch-wide rule failed) · TIMEOUT (2×verdict_timeout_ms, or G-20 clock failure)
— all three non-PASS outcomes are a HOLD, never a step to 0 for firm obligations (K7).
On PASS: sign_command_batch() (NEW) Ed25519-signs the JCS bytes of the CommandBatch's OWN
{batch_id, bank_id, epoch, seq, issued_at, expires_at, items} (interfaces/crypto.md §2.1) —
a SEPARATE signature from the verdict's own audit-trail signature in og.verdict; publishing
verdict.signature instead would fail every hub's BAD_SIGNATURE check — then publish the
signed CommandBatch and renew each item's hub Lease.
Guardian checks implemented
guardian/checks.py — numbering per 00-invariants.md
clock offset vs. NTP (K12) — runs first, alone
trace pre-image already written (K10)
batch on the DURABLE ledger version (K2, NEW fix)
epoch/seq/lease freshness, rechecked here (K6)
per-item: SoC + health=online to discharge (K1, NEW)
G-01-ENERGY
per-item: SoC over the FULL lease duration (K1)
per-item: |P| within inverter/hub cap (K4)
per-item: hub ramp bound (K4, shared w/ engine, NEW)
bank kVA loading from ADDED load only (K4/K9, NEW)
fleet-wide ramp cap, firm vs. non-firm (K4)
per-feeder/substation ramp ceiling, firm events (K4)
active L2 instruction is a hard boundary (K5)
commitment lock, scoped to NOW's interval (K13, NEW)
SAFE_STOP
an engaged stop (fleet/zone/bank) vetoes the batch
per-phase imbalance, PQ-sensitive only (K14, NEW)
THD voltage+current, PQ-sensitive only (K14, NEW)
freq/voltage deviation, PQ-sensitive (K14, NEW)
asset-state + ride-through conformance (K14, NEW)
calibration-command safety, bounds/rate (K14, NEW)
G-21..G-25: guardian/pq_checks.py (NEW, additive; diagram 06)
publish, QoS 1
6. MQTT — signed command batch + lease
og/v1/cmd/<bank_id>/batch · og/v1/lease/<hub_id> (retained)
command_batch.schema.json: {batch_id, bank_id, epoch, seq, issued_at, expires_at, items:
[{hub_id, p_kw_setpoint, reason_code}], key_id, signature}. lease.schema.json: {hub_id,
epoch, expires_at, issued_at} — retained, so a reconnecting hub sees its lease immediately.
7. Hub (og-sim-fleet): verify → apply or hold → ack
ogsim.fleet.commands — evaluate_batch()
Verify Ed25519 signature (crypto.md §2.1), THEN independently check epoch/seq/lease
freshness (K6) — an out-of-order or stale command is rejected even if correctly signed
Accepted → apply p_kw_setpoint (reserve/P/E-aware clip, ogsim.fleet.physics)
Lease expires with no fresh batch → hold the LAST signed setpoint (local autonomy, K7) —
never an unplanned step to 0 for a firm obligation
Publishes: ack/<hub_id> (QoS1, one per command) and tel/<zone>/<bank>/<hub> (QoS0, every
fleet.telemetry_interval_s = 2 s): {hub_id, soc_kwh, p_kw, health, seq, epoch, ...}
tel/#, ack/#, scada/#
8. og-engine ingests ack / telemetry (fleet twin)
opengrid.engine._mqtt_ingest_loop → opengrid.fleet
Subscribes tel/#, scada/#, scada/instruction/#, scada/wave/+/+/+/{summary,raw} (each payload
schema-validated before use); fleet.ingest_telemetry/ingest_scada_signal/ingest_utility_
instruction update the in-memory twin, then fleet.flush() upserts og.hub_state, COPYs og.
telemetry, and (NEW) writes og.command_ack (01fbd38) every engine tick — this is what stage 2's
next cycle reads as “now”. Wave summaries buffer + batch-flush, raw captures go to a background
worker (both NEW, diagram 06 stage 2).
og-guardian independently subscribes tel/# too, into its OWN cache (MqttHubStatePort) —
guardian's G-01/G-02/G-04 never trust the engine's copy of hub state (K2 independent check).
every settle.interval_s = 60 s
9. og-settle — metering, billing, P&L
opengrid.settle — metering.py, billing.py, profitability.py
meter_interval (from og.telemetry, source=DIRECT_HUB_METER) → performance (compliance vs.
threshold) → invoice_line (versioned, idempotent) → pnl (revenue − energy/degradation cost
− penalty). Depends on og.reservation for the obligation's committed amount — obligations now
reach COMMITTED/DELIVERING/FULFILLED/SHORTFALL (stage 3's fix, side note above), and (NEW,
289d68f) close_settled_obligations() now drives FULFILLED/SHORTFALL → SETTLED (R-SETTLED) once
every interval is metered/billed — the obligation lifecycle's last edge is now driven too.
